messages.subject: Re: allometry
parts:
Raquel,

This was a programming mishap that was resolved last week.  Please update geomorph from our github version,

devtools::install_github(‘geomorphR/geomorph’,ref=’Stable)

When we updated geomorph last, we forgot that the ANOVA table used in advanced.procD.lm now has one extra row, so the HOS test performed by procD.allometry now samples the wrong P-value on the CRAN version.  This was corrected on Github, but we will have to wait to update it on CRAN, as per their policy.

Best,
Mike


On Aug 11, 2018, at 10:05 AM, Raquel Mendes <raquel...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi Michael,

How are you doing?

Sorry to bother you, but Im trying to run an analysis on the new geomorph version, and I found a problem. When I run the procD.allometry function, it says that the null hypothesis of parallel slopes is supported, however the p-value for group allometries is always inferior to 0.05, even when i change the seed. When I plot using the PredLine method the slopes look indeed parallel. 

The data frame im using has 2 species, sex and season. I have try the analysis just for species and for species*sex and species*season. The problem appears in all 3 analysis: Parallel slopes in the plot, indication to accept the null hypothesis, but significant p-values for group allometries.

Also, i have rerun and old analysis with a different data frame (which had parallel slopes and p-values >0.05 in the old version) but now i find the same problem (slopes are still parallel but the p-value is <0.05).

Are the p-values being calculated correctly or am i missing something?

I send the data and part of the script.

Thank you.

Cheers,










Raquel Mendes
